newsitem.title: BERMUDA: UK's Clarke urges steps to end money laundering.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke urges steps to end money laundering.

text.p: Criminals must be stopped from laundering their dirty cash through Commonwealth countries, Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday.
"Money launderers are criminals. They must be stopped in their tracks, caught and punished," he said.
The issue is one of the key topics at a Commonwealth finance ministers meeting in this Caribbean island.
The 53-nation group of former members of the British Empire includes a number of tiny island states which earn their living as off-shore tax havens.
"Money laundering poses a serious threat to every Commonwealth member," Clarke told the meeting.
"Unless we take effective action to deter and punish money laundering, serious crime...will remain an attractive business proposition to criminals."
A just-completed international evaluation, which Clarke released here, praised Britain for its steps to prevent money laundering and said it could serve as a role model for other countries to follow.

Clarke proposed a series of steps to close off hiding places for dirty money, including the setting up of regional bodies to combat money lanudering and encourage the World Bank and International Monetary Fund to take more into account such controls when evaluating a member country economy.
There was no conflict between an effective system to combat the problem and liberalising financial markets, he said.

"On the contrary, increasingly all countries are finding that effective money laundering legislation is something they cannot afford to be without if they want to attract long-term flows from legitimate private business," he added.
